title: Weight Loss and Night Sweats
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy and constitutional B-symptoms (weight loss, night sweats, fever). Hodgkin's lymphoma is a B-cell malignancy defined by Reed-Sternberg cells — 'owl-eyed' nucleoli with clear cytoplasm, CD15+ and CD30+. Excisional lymph node biopsy (NOT FNA) is required for diagnosis to preserve architecture for immunophenotyping and cytogenetics. CXR is initial screening. PET/CT for staging: Stage I (single node), II (≥2 nodes same side of diaphragm), III (both sides), IV (extranodal). Treatment: ABVD chemotherapy (Adriamycin, Bleomycin, Vinblastine, Dacarbazine) ± radiation for early stage. Check albumin as prognostic indicator. Screen for HIV and EBV, which can mimic lymphoma.
chief_complaint: Painless cervical lymphadenopathy, weight loss, night sweats

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Full exam — symptoms concerning for malignancy.

stacks.label: HIV test
stacks.finding: HIV can present with lymphadenopathy and weight loss — must screen.

stacks.label: EBV titer
stacks.finding: EBV can cause enlarged lymph nodes and night sweats.

stacks.label: Chest X-ray
stacks.finding: Good initial screening tool. May show mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

stacks.label: CT abdomen/pelvis
stacks.finding: PET scan preferred over CT. CT if PET unavailable.

stacks.label: Urinalysis
stacks.finding: Good screening tool — cheap, easy, useful info.

stacks.label: Biopsy, lymph node (excisional)
stacks.finding: Excisional biopsy is required — NOT FNA. Need surrounding architecture for immunophenotyping and cytogenetics. Reed-Sternberg cells: CD15+, CD30+.

stacks.label: Albumin, serum
stacks.finding: Albumin is a prognostic indicator in Hodgkin's lymphoma.

stacks.label: CT chest / PET whole body
stacks.finding: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast for staging. PET provides metabolic information.

stacks.label: Consult, hematology/oncology
stacks.finding: Once diagnosis reached, consult heme/onc for treatment: ABVD chemotherapy ± radiation.

stacks.label: Counsel patient, cancer diagnosis
stacks.finding: Cancer diagnosis is devastating — go over next steps and what to expect.

physical_exam.general: Weight loss, night sweats — constitutional B-symptoms.
physical_exam.heent: Painless cervical lymphadenopathy — firm, rubbery, non-tender.

decoys.label: Fine-needle aspiration (FNA)
decoys.reason_wrong: FNA is insufficient for lymphoma diagnosis. Excisional biopsy is required — need intact architecture for Reed-Sternberg identification, immunophenotyping (CD15/CD30), and cytogenetics.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Reed-Sternberg cells are the hallmark of Hodgkin's lymphoma. FNA loses architecture needed for diagnosis. CD15+ and CD30+ on immunophenotyping.
Stage I: single node. II: ≥2 same side of diaphragm. III: both sides. IV: extranodal. Guides treatment intensity.
First-line: Adriamycin, Bleomycin, Vinblastine, Dacarbazine. Early stage: chemotherapy + radiation. Advanced: chemotherapy alone.

case_summary: Classic Hodgkin's lymphoma: painless cervical lymphadenopathy + B-symptoms. Excisional biopsy → Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15+/CD30+). PET/CT for staging. ABVD chemotherapy. Office diagnosis → heme/onc referral.
